text:
Maya (Sales): Heads-up - new POC with GlobalBank, fully air-gapped. They will not allow any outbound egress. Main asks: monthly patch cadence, emergency USB hotfixes, signed bundles, SBOM, HSM key attest. Need recommended SOW language + pricing uplift for sealed/offline delivery. Anyone seen a similar SOW?
Liam (Solutions): We've done this before. Approach: ship a signed minibundle (operator + runtime deltas) with SHA256 manifests. Option A: monthly delta bundles. Option B: quarterly full image + monthly deltas. Pricing: one-time sealed-bundle packaging fee + per-patch handling charge. I'll sketch numbers after we confirm patch cadence.
Sasha (Security): Security checklist items to confirm: SBOM per bundle, detached signatures (FIPS 140-2 acceptable), verification script that runs offline, and evidence of key custody (customer HSM preferred). No telemetry, so we need to surface how rollback proof is captured in logs.
Neal (R&D): Runtime constraints: we support incremental deltas for both operator and model artifacts. Need to ensure the customer keeps previous KV cache when applying deltas or we'll force full warm restart. Also we limit single-apply delta size to ~1.5GB by default to keep USB-able. If >1.5GB, we do chunked delta. Example bundle manifest (simplified):
```
bundle_id: redwood-offline-202603
base_image: rw-runtime:v2026.03.01
delta_from: rw-runtime:v2026.01.15
patches:
  - file: operator-delta-0001.tar.gz
    sha256: b2d9a3c9f5e2a8e3c9d4f0b6a1c3e2f9d7e5c6b1a2f3e4d5c6b7e8f9a0b1c2d3
  - file: model-quant-delta-0003.tar.gz
    sha256: a1c2d3e4f5b6c7d8e9f00112233445566778899aabbccddeeff00112233445566
signatures:
  - sigfile: bundle.sig
    signer: customer-ca or redwood-ca
```
Anna (Ops): Ops notes: recommended default cadence = monthly security/bug patches, quarterly feature bundle. Emergency hotfix process: customer receives a signed hotfix tar + verification script and an Ops runbook. We require a documented rollback path and compat matrix. Maintenance window expectation: 1-2 hours for delta apply. Hotfix SLA: 48-72 hours standard; accelerated available as add-on.
Maya (Sales): Legal/SecQ: they asked for completed security questionnaire sections about package signing and key custody. Sasha - can you own filling Sections 2 & 3? Also pricing: they asked for a firm per-patch line item.
Sasha (Security): Yep I'll fill those sections. Need the SBOM output (we generate SPDX), the signing workflow (we can sign with Redwood CA or accept customer-signed bundles), and confirmation on HSM options (we can integrate PKCS#11 in build pipeline). Note: if Redwood holds signing keys, customer will ask for key attestation and rotated keys policy.
Neal (R&D): If they want to sign locally, they need our manifest schema + a small verification binary we supply. That binary validates the detached sig and checks SBOM hashes before applying. Works fully offline.
deploy-bot: Artifact uploaded: artifacts/offline/1831235678/redwood-offline-bundle-v1.tar.gz (staging). SHA256: 9f8e7d6c5b4a39281726354433221100aaeebbccddee11223344556677889900
Anna (Ops): Operational constraints we should bake into SOW: max delta size per USB <= 1.5GB, retention of last 3 bundles on node, rollback preserved for 48hrs. For installers >1.5GB we do chunked apply; customer must supply USB/media/transfer method. Also note image provenance and SBOM must be retained for audits.
Liam (Solutions): For pricing framing: recommend line items - 1) Sealed bundle engineering fee (one-time), 2) per-patch handling & signing fee, 3) emergency hotfix premium (optional), 4) accelerated support SLA. I'll put numbers on this and send a sample SOW clause.
Maya (Sales): Perfect. Also they asked about upgrade cadence guarantees in the contract. We should propose: "We provide monthly security patches; feature rollouts scheduled quarterly; emergency fixes as defined by SLA." Is that acceptable?
Sasha (Security): That language is fine. Add: "Customer is responsible for offline transport and secure media storage; Redwood provides verification tools and signed artifacts."
Neal (R&D): One more technical ask: customer may want KMS integration for runtime key unwraps (model encryption). For fully air-gapped, we can support local HSM (PKCS#11) integration, but that requires ops support during initial bootstrap. Add to SOW as an optional professional service.
Maya (Sales): Great. Action items: Liam to draft SOW pricing lines; Sasha to fill security sections and attach SBOM template; Neal to produce manifest + verify binary; Anna to produce ops runbook excerpt and maintenance window language. I'll sync with GlobalBank on USB size constraints and timeline. :thumbsup:
Anna (Ops): I'll also prepare a short runbook snippet showing apply/verify/rollback commands (3 steps).
Maya (Sales): Thanks team - I'll loop in legal after we have draft numbers. If anyone finds any blockers (e.g., FIPS vs non-FIPS signing), flag here.
Sasha (Security): FYI - if they demand FIPS-only crypto for bundle signing we'll need validation on our side; that can add 2-3 weeks to compliance review. Flagged.
Liam (Solutions): Sending draft SOW by EOD tomorrow.
Maya (Sales): Awesome, thanks.
